title: Choose a runtime compatible with a native database driver
businessContext: Review a focused Next.js application change before it reaches production. The proposed file below contains the defect or unsupported assumption; external application services, where imported, are integration boundaries.
problemStatement: Review the proposed app/api/report/route.ts change. Identify the incorrect framework assumption, propose a minimal corrected implementation, and provide evidence for the selected version scope and its 15/16 differences. Explain the interview variation after solving the base task. This is a framework code review: actual rendering, routing and cache behavior must be checked in a real Next.js build, not a browser function sandbox.
constraints: Preserve the stated user behavior and keep trust boundaries explicit.
Use the selected version’s documented API; do not suppress build/type failures to hide the defect.
Build using the target deployment/runtime rather than only a local Node process.
Request with a present and absent temporary file.
Replace the file source with authorized durable storage for cross-instance requirements.
candidateTasks: Add actionable line-level review comments explaining impact and correction.
Write the corrected file in the local IDE copy; split annotated companion files where instructed.
Record actual build/request/navigation evidence against the acceptance checks and compare version notes.
hints: The Edge runtime does not provide the full Node.js API surface.

alternativeApproaches: No. Pool size, connection reuse and concurrent instance count still matter. Use an appropriate database proxy/pool strategy and measure connection saturation under scale-out.
commonMistakes: Verifying only next dev when the behavior depends on production rendering or bundling.
Treating a visible UI state, matcher or TypeScript type as a substitute for server-side validation and authorization.
